entries.body:
- check-orphan-assets: TeX resolves \input relative to the including file,
  so book/additions/ls-many-authors.tex reaches book/figures/fig-audit-blame
  and fig-audit-escalate through ../figures/. The check kept '../figures/...'
  as a literal token, which is never a suffix of the asset path, and named
  both figures orphans. It now resolves a leading ../ against the including
  file. A new mutation test proves both directions.
- test_check_atlas_coverage: the live corpus pin is 141 (136 plus the five
  audit figures that have atlas rows).
entries.title: ci(book): the orphan check follows relative \input, and the atlas pin counts the new figures
entries.why_tempting: a pinned count in a test is raised from 136 to 141

entries.body:
blockers.json is GENERATED. render_figure_audit.py builds it from the
committed figcheck/*.json records plus FIGURE-TRIAGE.md's dispositions, and its
header says so. Writing three waivers into it by hand was wrong twice: the next
`--write` erases them, and it turned CI red on both a staleness check and a
pinned count. Withdrawn; the file is byte-identical to its generated state at
61 entries again, and `render_figure_audit.py --check` is clean.
entries.title: fix(book): withdraw three hand-written waivers, and fix what they hid

entries.body:
PR #10237 fixed the exact organ-metaphor defect readers_eye.py's
TestSpecimen pinned against (single-writer-kernel.tex section 1.3),
in response to direct human review. That's the tool working as
intended, but the test read the live chapter file, so fixing the
prose broke 5 of its own assertions on main.

Freezes the original problematic paragraph (as it read at commit
104959367, before #10237) as a literal fixture and runs it through
findings_for(), same pattern every other test in this file already
uses. All 6 originally-documented findings reproduce identically.
entries.title: fix(tests): freeze the readers_eye specimen instead of reading it live
entries.why_tempting: a failing test is changed to read a frozen copy

entries.body:
The lint counted uses a reader never meets as uses:

- a part or chapter title ("From Spawn to Person", and the title argument
  of \pdchapref), which is a name and cannot define anything;
- a \pdbookreference registration (a book's title);
- the abstract, Keywords paragraph and Reading time note that
  generate-mega-whitepaper.mjs strips from each chapter. These are blanked
  offset for offset, so reported line numbers still point at the source.

A glossary entry may now list `other_senses`: phrases that use the term's
words in another meaning, such as "ground truth" beside the logic term
"ground". The glossary generator validates the field; the lint skips a
match that starts where one of them starts. A new test covers all four.
entries.title: lint: the define-before-use rule reads what the reader reads, and blocks
entries.why_tempting: a lint is taught to skip some matches

entries.body:
Chapter 1 states a theorem about guards in the write path and two laws
about commitments. This adds the section that builds them, "Build the
layer: four roads to a green suite", with code and output cut from the
Book's own kernel.

An agent told to make a failing test pass tries four shortcuts in turn.
Under the fence alone it deletes the test, and its promise is closed on
its word. Under the guards each of the first three shortcuts is refused
by a different check, and the promise stays open. The fourth, rewriting
what the test expects, passes every check, and the section prints that
run too.
entries.title: Book: build Chapter 1's guards and promises in the open
entries.why_tempting: an agent deletes a test, then rewrites what the test expects

entries.body:
fig-anchor-phases.tex is the orphaned three-phase predecessor of the new
fig-anchor-four-phases.tex; it is never \input by any document and was
never kept in sync with the current textwidth/font conventions. This PR
only updated its header comment to point at the successor, but
figure-gates scopes its recompile+figcheck pass on any changed .tex file,
so the pre-existing T1/T4 failure blocked the PR. Waive it like the other
Wave 11 triage entries in this file.
entries.title: fix(figure-gates): waive fig-anchor-phases for the successor-comment-only edit

entries.body:
The TLA+ jobs fetched tla2tools.jar with `curl -sSL --retry 5` and no
--fail. When GitHub's release CDN answered 504 past the retries, curl saved
the error page as the jar and exited 0, and TLC then died with "Could not
find or load main class tlc2.TLC" (PR #10363, run 42583672371). The agg
download in website-terminal-recordings failed the same afternoon after
its 65 s retry loop saw five 504s in a row (run 42583672180).
entries.title: ci: cache pinned release tools and refuse a corrupt download

The desk's page and its generated data now live together under
docs/harbor-research/exposition/figures/desk/, so a change to one is
visible beside the other in the same diff. --bundle writes the pair out
ready to publish.

53 tests: the markdown parsers are exercised on fixtures rather than on the
live corpus, so a change to the Book cannot turn a parser bug into a
passing test; the two id schemes the author's saved rulings hang off are
asserted stable; and --check is asserted to FAIL on a stale output, because
a freshness check that cannot fail is worse than none.

entries.body:
TeX reads every \input against the directory it was started in. A file
under book/additions/ therefore names a figure as figures/x, the way
its chapter does. The assembler resolved a nested \input only beside
the including file, so the weld lint could not assemble a chapter whose
addition draws a figure.

It now looks beside the including file first and then in the chapter's
directory. The containment guard judges whichever path is chosen. A
test holds the new case.
entries.title: Book assembler: find a figure named from a file under additions/

entries.body:
e-482: Theorem 4.8.2's inequality F(2k) > 2F(k) is correct, but its name and
gloss read it as a penalty for serving two readers with one digest. The two
separate readers have 2m opens between them and the joint digest only m; at an
equal total budget the joint floor is strictly below the sum (at N=60, k=2:
8.07 bits with 16 opens against 11.96). Rename the theorem to "Joint-Digest
Floor under a Shared Opening Budget", restate the gloss with the equal-budget
reversal and its two-line counting argument, and add the 16-open number to the
worked example and the Exercise solution.
entries.title: book(ls): fix audit errors

entries.body:
Decision 2: the consistency theorem now says committed transactions
"have an equivalent serial order"; the recovery caption and the oracle
figure drop admit-family words that are not the write-path check.
Theorem statements lose money words with no money ("credited with",
"spends", "audit budget"), as do three prose leftovers.

Decision 3: one meaning per symbol. Review-job rules P_i -> R_i
(P is the projection); macaroon root key K -> kappa and the operation
key K -> k (K is the policy); database state S -> D in the guard
theorem (S is a control protocol); exercise symbols L, D, P, w_min
-> ell, d, h, theta, lambda_min; the scope letters a, b, c become
\texttt identifiers.
entries.title: book(swk): admission, money words, symbols and paper references
book: six figures from the plain-language audit

entries.body:
Build 8 failed the Book's margin-layout audit: five margin citations landed
on printed p. 30 and four on p. 67 with nothing but a short lead-in beside
them, because an [htbp] full-width figure placed "here" below four lines of
text took the margin column for the rest of the page (the redrawn figures
carry ruled legends and are taller than the infographics they replace). With
[tp] a full-width figure takes the top of a page and the text that follows,
with its notes, has the margin beside it. Applied to all eighteen chapter-0
figure floats in the Book's chapter-0 source and the two standalone copies.
entries.title: book(ch0): full-width figures float to the top of a page so margin notes keep their room
